## 576. diagnose_ensemble_regression_with_individual_submissions  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** An ensemble regresses after changing or adding multiple component models simultaneously, and you cannot tell which component is responsible.
- **Action:** Submit each individual model's predictions separately to identify which models are strong and which are weak. Compare individual scores to the blend score. Then restore the blend using only confirmed-good components. This costs a few submissions but quickly reveals whether the regression comes from a specific model or from blend weights.
- **Exceptions:** Costly if submission budget is tight. Individual model LB scores may not perfectly predict blend contribution due to diversity effects.
- **Support:** kernels 49524919, 52860091; comps hms-harmful-brain-activity-c; tiers {'Grandmaster': 2}; episode reached new best: {'yes': 2}
- **Cells:** L3/explore/new_idea/part2
- **Examples:**
  - `49524919:e20#1` (hms-harmful-brain-ac, Grandmaster; steps 49524919:85->86, 49524919:86->87, 49524919:87->88): Submit each individual model's predictions separately (one submission per model) to identify which models are strong and which are weak. Compare individual scores to the blend score. This costs a few submissions but quickly reveals whether the regression comes from a specific model or from the blend weights. Then restore the blend using only confirmed-good components.
  - `52860091:e5#1` (hms-harmful-brain-ac, Grandmaster; steps 52860091:17->18, 52860091:19->20, 52860091:20->21, 52860091:21->22): First evaluate each candidate model variant in isolation to establish its standalone quality. Then test pairwise and higher-order combinations. If adding a variant worsens the ensemble despite being decent alone, try weighted blending before discarding it. If a variant is much stronger solo than others, test it alone before averaging — uniform averaging can dilute a strong model. Stop uniform-weight search when adding members hurts, and switch to weighted blending.

## 577. bracket_small_changes_with_reruns_to_estimate_noise  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** Leaderboard scores show high variance across identical re-runs (noise floor comparable to the effect size of changes being tested), such as single model swaps, threshold tweaks, or adding one ensemble member.
- **Action:** Bracket each small configuration change with at least one no-code re-run before and after to estimate the noise floor. Only trust an improvement that exceeds the observed re-run variance. If the change's effect is within the noise band, revert to the simpler configuration.
- **Exceptions:** When submission budget is very limited, a single confirming re-run may be all that's feasible (50376011 counter_evidence).
- **Support:** kernels 50376011, 52860091; comps hms-harmful-brain-activity-c; tiers {'Grandmaster': 2}; episode reached new best: {'yes': 1, 'no': 1}
- **Cells:** L3/explore/new_resource
- **Examples:**
  - `50376011:e22#2` (hms-harmful-brain-ac, Grandmaster; steps 50376011:108->109, 50376011:109->110, 50376011:113->114, 50376011:114->115): When testing small configuration changes (single model swap, threshold tweak), bracket each change with at least one no-code re-run before and after to estimate the noise floor. Only trust an improvement that exceeds the observed re-run variance. If a change's effect is within the noise band, revert to the simpler configuration.
  - `52860091:e9#1` (hms-harmful-brain-ac, Grandmaster; steps 52860091:47->48, 52860091:48->49, 52860091:50->51, 52860091:51->52): First submit the new models alone (or as a small blend) to gauge their standalone quality on the leaderboard. If they are substantially worse than the existing ensemble, do not expect them to help much when added. If standalone quality is reasonable, add them with small weight to the existing blend and increase weight only if LB improves. If the expanded blend cannot beat the previous best after 2-3 weight adjustments, abandon the new members.

## 578. ablate_ensemble_members_via_isolation  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** When an ensemble has accumulated many model families over time and recent additions may be degrading performance.
- **Action:** Test individual model groups in isolation by disabling all others, compare standalone scores to the full blend, then try the full blend minus suspected harmful members. The drop-one-out test is more informative than standalone scores alone, since individual ablation scores may all be worse than the full blend without revealing which member to drop.
- **Exceptions:** Individual isolation scores alone may not reveal which member to drop (49524919:e28#1); the full-blend-minus-one test is needed to confirm.
- **Support:** kernels 49524919, 50496431; comps hms-harmful-brain-activity-c; tiers {'Grandmaster': 2}; episode reached new best: {'yes': 2}
- **Cells:** L3/explore/plateau
- **Examples:**
  - `49524919:e28#1` (hms-harmful-brain-ac, Grandmaster; steps 49524919:130->131, 49524919:131->132, 49524919:132->133, 49524919:133->134): Test individual model groups in isolation by disabling all others (using continue statements or similar), compare their standalone scores to the full blend score, then re-enable all groups that individually perform reasonably while permanently removing groups that consistently underperform. The final configuration should be the full blend minus identified harmful members.
  - `50496431:e31#1` (hms-harmful-brain-ac, Grandmaster; steps 50496431:101->102, 50496431:102->103, 50496431:103->104): First strip the ensemble down to a minimal set (even one model) with simple mean blending to establish a clean baseline. Then upgrade the target component in isolation. Finally, re-add it to the full ensemble. This isolates the effect of the upgrade before committing to the blend. Accept temporary score regressions during isolation steps.

## 579. toggle_preprocessing_factors_individually_on_large_regression  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** When a new inference pipeline has multiple preprocessing differences from a known-good one and produces a large regression.
- **Action:** Toggle each changed preprocessing factor one at a time, submitting or checking validation after each. Start by enabling the factor most likely to match training conditions. If a factor consistently hurts across multiple checkpoints, disable it permanently. Limit to 3-4 experiments before deciding.
- **Exceptions:** 55621328:e10#1 notes v19→v20 changed two factors simultaneously, making attribution harder; sometimes practical constraints force bundling.
- **Support:** kernels 55621328, 58130512; comps learning-agency-lab-automate; tiers {'Master': 2}; episode reached new best: {'no': 2}
- **Cells:** L3/explore/regression
- **Examples:**
  - `55621328:e10#1` (learning-agency-lab-, Master; steps 55621328:18->19, 55621328:19->20, 55621328:21->22): Toggle each changed preprocessing factor one at a time (or in small groups), submitting or checking validation after each change. Start by enabling the factor most likely to match training conditions. If a factor consistently hurts across multiple checkpoints, disable it permanently. Limit to 3-4 experiments before deciding.
  - `58130512:e25#1` (learning-agency-lab-, Master; steps 58130512:74->75, 58130512:76->77): When exploring coupled CV/postprocessing choices, change at most one axis per submission. If a change causes a large regression (>0.005), immediately revert it in the next version. Keep a known-good configuration as the anchor and return to it after each failed experiment. Do not change numeric hyperparameters simultaneously with structural CV changes.

## 580. reorder_data_merge_by_id  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** Data is reordered for batching efficiency (e.g., sorting by sequence length) before inference.
- **Action:** Always track reordered IDs explicitly and merge predictions back to the submission by ID rather than relying on positional alignment. If a catastrophic regression occurs after adding sorting, check alignment first before reverting the sorting change.

Never submit a stacking change without validating locally first.

## 581. restore_production_settings_before_tuning  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** You have been iterating with reduced settings for speed (fewer folds, cached preprocessing, subset of data) and now have a working pipeline with a baseline score.
- **Action:** Before tuning new levers, restore all settings you weakened for iteration speed (fold count, data size, ensemble members). Submit to confirm the restored setting matches or exceeds your baseline. This establishes the true baseline before further optimization.

## 582. oof_predictions_stored_before_postprocessing  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** OOF predictions are being stored after transformations (clipping, rounding, offsets) that should only apply to final submissions, potentially corrupting CV evaluation.
- **Action:** Before tuning any post-processing step, ensure OOF predictions are stored in their raw form immediately after model prediction, before any clipping or rounding. This is a prerequisite for trusting calibration experiments and CV metrics.

## 583. test_new_model_standalone_before_ensemble_integration  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** When a new model variant or modality is available and its quality relative to existing ensemble members is unknown.
- **Action:** First test the new model in isolation to get its standalone leaderboard score. If standalone quality is far worse than the ensemble, it is unlikely to help when blended. Limit checkpoint sweeps to 2-3 variants before deciding to abandon or integrate. If standalone is reasonable, add it to the full ensemble and submit.
- **Exceptions:** 52551258:e8#1 notes weak standalone models can still improve ensembles via diversity, so don't discard solely based on standalone score.

If the standalone score is far worse than the current ensemble best, the component is unlikely to help when blended. Limit checkpoint sweeps to 2-3 variants before deciding to abandon or integrate.
  - `52551258:e8#1` (hms-harmful-brain-ac, Expert; steps 52551258:14->15, 52551258:15->16): First test the new model in isolation to gauge its standalone quality. If it regresses badly alone, immediately combine it with existing members rather than discarding it—weak standalone models can still improve ensembles. Re-enable all members and submit to confirm the combined effect.

## 584. reduce_cv_folds_for_slow_exploratory_runs  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** When trying a slow algorithm variant (e.g., DART boosting) that may not pay off, and you have per-fold metrics available.
- **Action:** Reduce CV folds to 2 for a quick probe. Inspect per-fold validation scores. If the idea doesn't clearly beat the baseline on those folds, revert the risky change while keeping any ancillary improvements. Then restore full CV folds and submit.
- **Exceptions:** 2-fold CV is noisy; the quick probe may misjudge the idea's potential due to high variance.
- **Support:** kernels 27389424, 27656049; comps amex-default-prediction; tiers {'Grandmaster': 1, 'Expert': 1}; episode reached new best: {'no': 1, 'yes': 1}

  - `27656049:e7#1` (amex-default-predict, Expert; steps 27656049:19->20, 27656049:22->23): Reduce CV folds to 2 for a quick probe of the new idea. Inspect per-fold validation scores. If the idea doesn't clearly beat the baseline on those folds, revert the risky change while keeping any ancillary improvements (e.g., class weighting, hyperparams). Then restore full CV folds and submit.

## 585. marginal_regression_keep_and_move_on  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** When a probe yields a marginal LB regression (within noise range, e.g., <0.001) and either CV scores are available as a second signal or higher-impact levers remain untapped.
- **Action:** Do not automatically revert a sub-noise-threshold regression. Cross-reference with CV if available; if CV is neutral or positive, keep the change. If no CV is available but larger gains are available from other levers, accept the marginal regression without reverting and move on to higher-impact experiments. Reserve reverts for clear regressions visible in both CV and LB.
- **Exceptions:** none
- **Support:** kernels 27836972, 28093671; comps amex-default-prediction; tiers {'Expert': 1, 'Contributor': 1}; episode reached new best: {'no': 2}
- **Cells:** L3/probe/new_idea/part4
- **Examples:**
  - `27836972:e5#2` (amex-default-predict, Expert; steps 27836972:26->27): Do not automatically revert a change that causes a sub-0.001 LB regression. Cross-reference with CV score. If CV is neutral or positive, keep the change and move on to the next experiment. Reserve reverts for clear regressions visible in both CV and LB.
  - `28093671:e11#2` (amex-default-predict, Contributor; steps 28093671:42->43): Accept the marginal regression without reverting or further tuning the tested lever. Move on to higher-impact levers. Only revisit minor ensemble tuning after larger gains are exhausted.

## 586. avoid_bundling_features_with_infrastructure  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** When adding a new feature source (e.g., embeddings, new columns) and simultaneously changing infrastructure (GPU mode, n_estimators, code restructuring).
- **Action:** Do not bundle new features with infrastructure changes in the same submission. Submit the feature addition alone first to isolate its effect. If it regresses, you know the features are the cause. If you must change infrastructure, do it in a separate prior submission to establish a clean baseline.
- **Exceptions:** none

If the score drops, abandon or apply dimensionality reduction before retrying. Do not bundle the new features with infrastructure changes (e.g., GPU mode) that could mask the signal.

## 587. checkpoint_selection_via_val_loss_then_lb_verify  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** When multiple trained checkpoints (different epochs, training runs, or configurations) are available and can be swapped at inference time with zero cost.
- **Action:** Compare validation losses across available checkpoints and select the set with better per-fold val losses. Submit once to verify on the leaderboard. Do not sweep many checkpoint combinations—use val loss as a proxy to pick one candidate, then verify. If per-fold val losses are mixed (some folds better, some worse), still submit for LB verification since ensemble-level performance may differ from per-fold signals.
- **Exceptions:** Per-fold val loss is not a perfect proxy for ensemble LB score (50496431:e2#2 showed mixed fold losses but overall LB improvement).
- **Support:** kernels 49524919, 50496431; comps hms-harmful-brain-activity-c; tiers {'Grandmaster': 2}; episode reached new best: {'no': 1, 'yes': 1}

If the probe regresses meaningfully, abandon that variant immediately and return to the incumbent. Do not sweep hyperparameters for the new variant unless the probe is competitive.
  - `50496431:e2#2` (hms-harmful-brain-ac, Grandmaster; steps 50496431:7->8): Compare validation losses across available checkpoints and swap in the set with better per-fold val losses. Submit to verify on the leaderboard. If the new checkpoints improve the score, keep them and move on to a different lever. Do not sweep many checkpoint combinations—use val loss as a reliable proxy to pick one candidate set, then verify once.

## 588. revert_large_feature_batch_on_regression  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** When adding a large batch of new features causes a leaderboard regression and one or two compensating tweaks fail to recover the prior best score.
- **Action:** Revert the feature addition entirely rather than continuing to tune around it. Do not spend more than two recovery attempts. If the features are believed to contain some useful signals, consider adding them in smaller subsets in future probes rather than all at once.

## 589. add_new_member_to_uniform_ensemble_then_tune_weights  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** An ensemble uses uniform averaging and a new prediction source is available. Prior additions of diverse sources have yielded small LB improvements.
- **Action:** Add the new prediction source to the uniform average (adjusting the denominator), submit once. If the score improves, keep the member and then move to weight tuning as a separate step. Do not tune weights and membership simultaneously. If weight tuning regresses, revert to uniform weights.

The newest component is the least optimized and has the most room for improvement.

If the score improves, keep the member and move to weight tuning. If it regresses, remove it. Do not tune weights and membership simultaneously.

## 592. ensemble_new_best_member_with_previous_best  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** A newly tested single model outperforms the previous best single model, and ensembling has historically helped in this pipeline.
- **Action:** Immediately test combining the new best member with the previous best member. If the pair beats both individuals, keep the pair. If not, keep the better individual. This one-step greedy addition is cheap and almost always worth trying before exploring further combinations.
- **Exceptions:** none

If the pair beats both individuals, keep the pair. If not, keep the better individual. This one-step greedy addition is cheap and almost always worth trying before exploring further.

## 593. noisy_lb_continue_sweep_before_reverting  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** The public leaderboard has very few evaluation rows (e.g., <10), making individual submission scores very noisy, and a small regression occurs after toggling an ensemble member.
- **Action:** Do not immediately revert a small regression. Continue the sweep to cover all candidate members. After the sweep, select the best-scoring configuration rather than greedily reverting each regression. This avoids being misled by noise on individual submissions.
- **Exceptions:** none

If two consecutive submissions regress, reverse the last member change rather than continuing in the same direction. Stop after 3-4 attempts without improvement—noisy LB signal means further tuning is overfitting to public scores.

After the sweep, select the best-scoring configuration rather than greedily reverting each regression. This avoids being misled by noise on individual submissions.

## 594. persist_through_noise_if_direction_justified  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** A hyperparameter change causes a small regression that is within the leaderboard noise margin, and you have theoretical or empirical reason to believe the direction is correct (e.g., underfitting evidence).
- **Action:** Check whether the change was fully and consistently applied before reverting. Complete the intended modification and submit again rather than immediately abandoning the direction. Only abandon after a clean, complete application still shows regression.
- **Exceptions:** If the regression is large (clearly exceeding noise), revert immediately rather than persisting.
- **Support:** kernels 55591012, 55621328; comps learning-agency-lab-automate; tiers {'Grandmaster': 1, 'Master': 1}; episode reached new best: {'yes': 2}
- **Cells:** L3/sweep/new_idea/part3

Complete the intended modification and submit again rather than immediately abandoning the direction.
  - `55621328:e4#2` (learning-agency-lab-, Master; steps 55621328:7->8): After a regression, test a simple baseline (e.g., naive rounding) to establish a lower bound and confirm the lever matters. Then move to improving the upstream signal (better model, better features) rather than continuing to sweep the same post-processing parameter, since small threshold changes have diminishing returns compared to model improvements.

## 595. hp_tuning_before_feature_engineering_budget  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** When HP tuning yields small incremental gains on a simple feature set and the gap to top scores is large, suggesting feature engineering has more headroom.
- **Action:** Spend at most 2-3 submissions on hyperparameter tuning to capture easy gains, then switch to feature engineering. Resume HP tuning only after the feature set is enriched. If each HP step yields diminishing improvements relative to the gap to top scores, that confirms the feature set is the bottleneck.
- **Exceptions:** 28093671:e8#2 shows that when each bundled change yields clear improvement, escalating magnitude (e.g., use all features) is preferable to many small increments.
- **Support:** kernels 27656049, 28093671; comps amex-default-prediction; tiers {'Expert': 1, 'Contributor': 1}; episode reached new best: {'yes': 2}
- **Cells:** L3/sweep/new_idea/part4
- **Examples:**
  - `27656049:e3#2` (amex-default-predict, Expert; steps 27656049:8->9, 27656049:9->10): Spend at most 2-3 submissions on hyperparameter tuning to capture easy gains, then switch to feature engineering. If each HP step yields diminishing or small improvements relative to the gap to top scores, that confirms the feature set is the bottleneck. Resume HP tuning only after the feature set is enriched.
  - `28093671:e8#2` (amex-default-predict, Contributor; steps 28093671:34->35, 28093671:35->36, 28093671:36->37): Bundle complementary changes (feature additions with compatible hyperparameter adjustments) into single submissions. If each bundle improves, escalate the magnitude of the next change. When gains are consistently positive, push to the logical extreme (e.g., use all available features) rather than making many small increments. Stop escalating when you've exhausted the lever's range.

## 596. measure_noise_floor_before_tuning  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** When leaderboard scores fluctuate significantly across identical or near-identical re-runs, or when the public test set is very small.
- **Action:** Submit the same unchanged code multiple times (5-10) to measure run-to-run variance. Only treat score differences larger than the observed variance as signal. When variance is high, prefer ensembles or averaged submissions over single-model runs, and do not chase improvements smaller than the noise floor.
- **Exceptions:** 50376011:e21#1 notes that high variance can occasionally be exploited by cherry-picking favorable runs, though this is unreliable.
- **Support:** kernels 50376011, 50496431; comps hms-harmful-brain-activity-c; tiers {'Grandmaster': 2}; episode reached new best: {'no': 2}
- **Cells:** L3/sweep/new_idea/part4
- **Examples:**
  - `50376011:e21#1` (hms-harmful-brain-ac, Grandmaster; steps 50376011:97->98, 50376011:98->99, 50376011:99->100, 50376011:100->101): Before drawing conclusions from config changes, submit the same unchanged code multiple times (5-10) to measure the run-to-run variance. Only treat score differences larger than the observed variance as signal. When variance is high, prefer ensembles or averaged submissions over single-model runs, and do not chase small improvements by toggling configs.
  - `50496431:e23#1` (hms-harmful-brain-ac, Grandmaster; steps 50496431:75->76, 50496431:76->77): Toggle the setting off, submit, then toggle it back on and submit. Compare the three scores (before, off, on). If the difference is within noise (~0.001), treat the setting as neutral and move to higher-impact levers. If re-enabling produces a worse score than the original, suspect non-determinism and do not trust the comparison without a third confirmation run.

## 597. probe_opposite_direction_after_regression  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** When a directional hyperparameter change (e.g., lowering learning rate) causes a leaderboard regression, and the optimal direction is unknown.
- **Action:** Explore the opposite direction with a large step to establish bounds (overshoot deliberately). Use fast local validation for exploratory runs. Once both directions have been probed, narrow in on the best region and submit only the refined candidate. This brackets the optimum with minimal LB submissions.
- **Exceptions:** none
- **Support:** kernels 27389424, 27825577; comps amex-default-prediction; tiers {'Grandmaster': 1, 'Expert': 1}; episode reached new best: {'no': 1, 'yes': 1}
- **Cells:** L3/sweep/new_idea/part5
- **Examples:**
  - `27389424:e2#1` (amex-default-predict, Grandmaster; steps 27389424:10->11, 27389424:11->12, 27389424:12->13, 27389424:13->14): First sweep coarsely in one direction (e.g., doubling: 1→2→5→10→25→50→100) using fast debug runs. If validation degrades or plateaus, reverse direction and sweep the opposite side of the baseline with decreasing step sizes. Use local CV with the competition metric as the signal. If the entire range shows no clear winner, abandon the lever and move on.
  - `27825577:e3#2` (amex-default-predict, Expert; steps 27825577:6->7, 27825577:7->8, 27825577:8->9, 27825577:9->10): After a regression from moving a parameter in one direction, explore the opposite direction with a large step to establish bounds (overshoot deliberately). Use fast validation (not LB submission) for these exploratory runs. Once both directions have been probed, narrow in on the best region and submit only the refined candidate. This brackets the optimum with minimal LB submissions.

## 598. submit_partial_configs_after_long_dev  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** After a long development/debugging phase (10+ versions) building a complex new feature pipeline without beating the previous best score.
- **Action:** Submit partial configurations with systematic toggling (feature on/off, selection on/off) across 3-5 submissions to identify which components contribute before combining everything. ## 599. validate_new_component_locally_before_submitting  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** You are integrating a new model, feature source, or pipeline component that requires code changes and may introduce bugs.

## 600. fix_data_pipeline_bugs_before_weight_tuning  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** A model that should be strong based on standalone performance is performing poorly within an ensemble, and you suspect a data/preprocessing mismatch (e.g., shape mismatch, wrong normalization).
- **Action:** Inspect the data pipeline for shape mismatches, preprocessing inconsistencies, or dead code before continuing the weight search. Fix the bug, then re-run the best-known ensemble configuration to get a clean baseline before further tuning.

If the score still doesn't improve, the checkpoint itself is the problem.

## 601. upgrade_components_when_blend_tuning_regresses  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** When ensemble blend weight tuning alone causes regression or plateaus, and the component model predictions themselves may be suboptimal or stale.
- **Action:** Stop tuning blend weights on stale predictions. Upgrade the underlying component model predictions (retrained or improved versions), then retune blend weights jointly with the new components. Verify with a submission before iterating further.

If LB improves, record it and continue exploring nearby configurations. If LB declines for 2-3 consecutive attempts with different configurations, stop sweeping weights and instead add a new diverse model to the pool before resuming.

## 602. diagnose_bug_before_abandoning_direction  [L3]  —  2 kernels, 1 comps, 2 items

- **Context:** When a structural code change (architecture refactor, new branch, not just a hyperparameter) causes a regression.
- **Action:** Inspect the changed forward pass or pipeline for correctness bugs (e.g., operations applied to wrong tensor, missing ensemble member, disabled component) before reverting the entire change. Fix the bug and re-evaluate. Only abandon the direction if the corrected version still regresses.
- **Exceptions:** none
- **Support:** kernels 49524919, 50496431; comps hms-harmful-brain-activity-c; tiers {'Grandmaster': 2}; episode reached new best: {'yes': 1, 'no': 1}

Fix the bug and re-evaluate with the same or nearby checkpoints. Only abandon the direction if the corrected version still regresses.

If the score does not recover to the previous best, the problem may be that disabling a model component was harmful.
